canonical_title: Narrow, single-finding correction scope with finding-scoped independent re-verification resolves complex failure chains without re-litigating settled work
summary: Stage 5 of SB-ORG-LEARNING-1.1 needed seven sequential correction rounds (S5-F-01 through S5-F-07) before an independent PASS. Each round authorized correction of exactly one newly-discovered finding, preserved all previously resolved findings unchanged, and required the independent verifier to re-check only the new finding plus a fixed regression set -- never a full re-litigation of already-passed work. This pattern let a genuinely hard, multi-layered filesystem-safety defect (unsafe absence detection) be resolved incrementally and verifiably instead of through one large, harder-to-verify rewrite.

claims.text: Stage 5 required seven distinct narrow-correction authorizations (S5-F-01/F-02 combined, then F-05, F-06, F-07 each separately), each one explicitly scoped to correct only the newly reproduced finding while explicitly preserving all prior corrections, ending in an independent PASS disposition.

evidence.locator: Section 3, 'Correction authority': 'Claude Code is authorized to correct only the four findings above... This is a correction inside the existing bounded reconciliation architecture.'

Section 1, 'Decision and authority': 'S5-F-07 is independently resolved... S5-F-01 through S5-F-06 remain resolved within the verified boundary; no regression blocker remains within the authorized Stage 5 scope.'

claims.text: Each Stage 5 correction round found and fixed a narrower, more specific defect than the previous round believed it had fully closed: S5-F-05 fixed a dangling-final-entry absence check, S5-F-06 found that fix still trusted an unvalidated ancestor, and S5-F-07 found that even the S5-F-06 fix still trusted a null-ancestor result as absence -- each correction was a small, targeted addition to the prior one, never a rewrite.

evidence.locator: Section 4, 'Null-ancestor correction': 'One-line, smallest-possible change... reusing the exact same status/condition/fail-closed path the S5-F-06 found-but-invalid-ancestor branch already uses. No new reconciliation state.'

conditions: Applies when an independent verifier can cheaply re-check a fixed regression set plus one new finding, rather than needing to re-run an expensive full review every round.
Requires the correction authority (Mission Control) to explicitly name the single finding in scope and explicitly list what must remain unchanged, so the builder cannot silently widen scope.
anti_patterns: Bundling multiple unrelated findings into one large correction pass, which forces the independent verifier to re-derive the entire failure surface from scratch and makes it harder to isolate which specific change fixed which specific defect.

Treating a corrected finding as fully closed without an independent re-verification pass scoped to that exact finding -- three of the seven S5 findings (F-05, F-06, F-07) were each discovered only because the prior 'complete' fix was independently re-examined rather than accepted on the builder's own claim.
